newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels deny abandoning demand to free comrades.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels deny abandoning demand to free comrades.

text.p: The leader of Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages, denying they were retreating from their key demand, reiterated on Monday the rebels want jailed guerrilla members released before they will free their captives.
Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said last weekend rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) "implicitly" accepted putting aside their central demand.

MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa told the CBS Telenoticias network on Monday rebels have had "informal conversations" with Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani, a member of a committee agreed by rebels to mediate negotiations.
However, "it is absolutely false that we have renounced our request for the freedom of our comrades, which will have to be addressed in eventual talks," Cerpa said via walkie-talkie.
The roughly 15 armed rebels have held the hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence for 48 days.

Most of the hostages seized on Dec. 17 were released, but the rebels kept those they considered the most important bargaining chips, including Fujimori's brother, two Peruvian cabinet ministers and about 25 Japanese businessmen and diplomats.
